title: Streetwear Accessories: Three Is the Limit, Four Kills the Fit
description: Cap, crossbody bag, chain and socks decide whether a fit reads expensive or cluttered. The rule of three, plus four mistakes to fix before you go out.
excerpt: It's rarely the tee or the shoes that ruin a fit. It's the fourth accessory.
content:
Streetwear basics are simple: tee, trousers, shoes. What separates "that looks good" from "that looks like a costume" is almost always the accessories — and specifically how many of them you're wearing at once.

## The rule of three

Three statement accessories per outfit, maximum. Cap, crossbody bag, chain — done. Add a logo watch, a beaded bracelet and sunglasses parked on your forehead, and the fit loses its focal point and starts reading like a shop window.

Quick test: take a mirror photo and look at it for half a second. Where did your eye land first? If the answer is nowhere in particular, you're wearing too much.

## The cap decides your head shape

Unstructured caps (soft crown, dad cap) suit almost everyone and sit well with relaxed fits. A structured five-panel or snapback holds its shape and reads sharper — but it adds volume if your face is on the rounder side. Curve the brim slightly. And take the sticker off; that joke retired around 2015.

## Crossbody bags have exactly one good position

Across the chest, strap over the shoulder, bag sitting around rib height. Around the waist only works with wider trousers and a longer hoodie. Above all, don't overstuff it — a bulging bag looks like a first-aid kit.

## Socks are an accessory, not underwear

White ankle socks with low sneakers, ribbed crew socks with shorts and high tops. Thin black dress socks with sneakers are the fastest way to drag down an otherwise solid outfit.
